Jim stood in the center of the advanced yoga studio, his face a mask of determination and impending doom. He had intended to join the beginner’s flow, but a misread schedule had landed him in the "Advanced Inversions & Zen Silence" session. The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity, glided past him with a gentle smile that didn't quite reach her eyes.

"Find your center, Jim," she whispered.

Jim tried to find his center, but his center was currently occupied by a burrito he had eaten for lunch. He attempted a simple Triangle Pose, but his long, lanky limbs got tangled in a way that defied geometry. As he wobbled precariously, he let out a low, guttural grunt. The class, a group of yogis who had spent years mastering the art of silent breathing, flinched in unison.

"Deeper into the stretch, Jim," Serenity instructed.

Jim pushed harder. His body, unaccustomed to such advanced flexibility, rebelled. He twisted his torso, trying to reach his foot, but the movement compressed his abdomen with the force of a hydraulic press. A sound escaped him—not a grunt this time, but a sharp, resonant *toot* that echoed off the studio walls like a foghorn in a library.

The silence that followed was absolute. Every eye in the room turned to Jim. He froze, his leg still extended, his face burning hotter than a hot yoga room.

"Excellent release of tension," Serenity said, her voice trembling slightly. "Now, let us move into the Long Neck Pose."

Jim blinked. "The what?"

"The Long Neck Pose," she repeated, demonstrating by stretching her neck upward, imitating a specific animal. "It requires immense control and stillness. It is known for its long neck."

Jim looked around. The other students were staring at him, waiting for him to mimic the pose. He didn't know which animal was known for its long neck, but he knew he needed to blend in. He remembered seeing one at the zoo once. He slowly raised his chin, stretching his neck as far as it would go, trying to look like a graceful creature.

But as he held the pose, the pressure on his stomach returned. He tried to hold his breath, to maintain the zen, but the burrito had other plans. Another sound escaped, this one longer and more melodic, vibrating through his elongated neck
